correctness.rationale: The Abrams cubical 2-particle complex applies to a 3-connected planar prism n>=5. Ko–Park Theorem 3.16 gives first Betti n+2 and an oriented exchange line, while an equivariant total-motion map onto H1(P_n) identifies the face permutation module twisted by orientation; the Y-exchange sign is eps⊠tau. On the cubical chains, every 0-,1-,2-cell fixed by rotation, reflection or layer swap has explicitly signed trace, with a minus sign when a pair of oriented edges is exchanged. Equivariant Euler–Poincaré gives χ_H2=T0−T1+T2−1+χ_H1=χ_{∧²U_n}−eps+(-1)^c; the removable eps has floor((n−1)/2)>=2 actual multiplicity. Exact integral H2 is free as kernel of a free-chain boundary, and H1 is free by the planar theorem. Character averages give the three quotient Betti lists. Independently built signed-cell traces for all 180 D_n×C2 elements at n=5..10 matched the group-character formula; these finite examples do not replace universal conjugacy-type trace formulas or the Ko–Park premise.
